mainTopic: Food cooked without an עירוב תבשילין, how many dishes the עירוב needs, and immersing before a יום טוב that falls after שבת
overview: The amud opens with a question: if someone cooked or baked on יום טוב for שבת without an עירוב תבשילין, may the food be eaten? The גמרא tries many proofs that the food is forbidden: the ברייתא's silence, a ruling about הערמה, and cases of tithing, immersing vessels, and cooking on שבת done on purpose. Each proof is pushed away. A ברייתא teaches only permitted solutions, הערמה is treated more strictly, the strict ברייתא may follow בית שמאי, and in the other cases the loss is small or שבת is more severe. So the question is not decided. Next the גמרא brings רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's different version of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about two dishes. רבא rules like our משנה and בית הלל: one cooked dish is enough. אביי adds that if you began your dough and the עירוב was eaten afterward, you may finish. A new משנה then discusses immersing people and vessels when יום טוב falls right after שבת. The גמרא begins asking why vessels may not be immersed on שבת. רבה starts to answer that it is a גזרה, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If baking anyway were allowed, the ברייתא should have said so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the earlier ברייתא gave only a workaround. If baking without an עירוב were simply permitted after the fact, the ברייתא should have said 'if he baked, it is permitted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If it really were permitted, the ברייתא should have taught: if he went ahead and baked, the bread is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that food baked without an עירוב תבשילין is forbidden. Its point is that the ברייתא never says it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא offered a legal workaround for someone with no עירוב. If baking anyway still left the bread permitted, that would be the simplest thing to say. Because the ברייתא is silent about it, the גמרא suggests the bread must be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach (the ברייתא should have said)
He went against the rule and baked
Food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: And if it is so (that it is permitted),
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier ברייתא, which gave a permitted workaround for someone with no עירוב.

phrases.english: let it teach: if he transgressed and baked, it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a proof attempt from the earlier ברייתא on this דף.
steps.raayaObject: That food baked on יום טוב for שבת without an עירוב is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier ברייתא does not say 'if he baked, it is permitted.'

steps.title: The ברייתא teaches only permitted solutions
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה explains that a ברייתא teaches ways to fix a problem that are permitted. It does not teach a fix that involves doing something forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said: The תנא teaches a permitted solution. He does not teach a solution that involves doing something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה pushes away the proof. The ברייתא's silence does not show that the bread is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking without an עירוב is forbidden to do in the first place, even if the bread might be allowed afterward. A תנא would not offer 'go ahead and break the rule' as a solution. So his silence proves nothing about whether the bread may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said:
the tanna teaches a remedy that is permitted,
a remedy that is forbidden, he does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה: תַּנָּא, תַּקַּנְתָּא דְהֶיתֵּרָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof drawn from the ברייתא's silence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא would not offer a forbidden act as a solution, so its silence tells us nothing about the result after the fact.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: the rules when the עירוב is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. With an עירוב, a person may bake, cook and insulate food. If he ate the עירוב before doing so, he may not cook at all, and others may not cook for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone who set up an עירוב תבשילין may bake, cook and insulate food. If he wants to eat his עירוב, he may. If he ate it before he baked or insulated, he may not bake, cook or insulate, not for himself and not for others. Others may also not bake or cook for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second proof with a new ברייתא. This first part sets up the background, and the key line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the עירוב has been eaten before any cooking began, it no longer works, so cooking for שבת is forbidden. This sets up the case the ברייתא goes on to discuss: a person with no working עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof from a source)
Insulates (wraps food to keep it warm)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
one who placed an eiruv tavshilin —
he may bake and cook and insulate,
and if he wants to eat his eiruv —
he has permission.

phrases.aramaic: אֲכָלוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא אָפָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִטְמִין —
phrases.english: If he ate it before he baked, before he insulated —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יֹאפֶה וְלֹא יְבַשֵּׁל וְלֹא יַטְמִין,
phrases.english: he may not bake, nor cook, nor insulate,
neither for himself nor for others.
And others may not bake or cook for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהִנִּיחַ עֵירוּבֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That food cooked for שבת without a working עירוב is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an עירוב that was eaten; the key line follows in step 4.

steps.title: Food made through trickery is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. He may cook for יום טוב, and leftovers may be kept for שבת, as long as he does not use הערמה. If he did use הערמה, the food is forbidden. This looks like proof that cooking without an עירוב makes the food forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he may cook for יום טוב. If some is left over, it is left over for שבת, as long as he does not trick the rule. If he did trick it, the food is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the proof. Food cooked for שבת without an עירוב, through trickery, is forbidden to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pretending to cook for יום טוב while really cooking for שבת is a sneaky way of cooking for שבת without an עירוב. The ברייתא forbids that food. The גמרא wants to learn from this that any food cooked for שבת without an עירוב is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Use trickery (to get around a rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: This clause is the heart of the proof. If food cooked without an עירוב through הערמה is forbidden, the גמרא hopes to show that food cooked without an עירוב is forbidden in general.

phrases.english: But he may cook for the Festival,
and if he left over — he has left over for Shabbat,
provided that he does not use trickery.
And if he used trickery — it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: The food itself becomes forbidden to eat. That is what the גמרא wants to prove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 3 and gives the line the proof depends on.
steps.raayaObject: Food cooked for שבת without an עירוב is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'וְאִם הֶעֱרִים אָסוּר' — food made by trickery is forbidden.

steps.title: Trickery is treated more strictly than sinning on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof. The חכמים were stricter about הערמה than about someone who cooks on purpose, so the ברייתא tells us nothing about the plain sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You are talking about trickery. Trickery is different, because the חכמים were stricter about it than about someone who sins on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes away the second proof. He says the ברייתא's case is a special, stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that if trickery makes the food forbidden, then plainly cooking against the rule surely does too. רב אשי reverses this: the חכמים punished הערמה more harshly than a מזיד. So the food of someone who simply cooked on purpose may still be permitted, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Trickery; getting around a rule with a cover story

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume trickery is milder than open sinning. Here the חכמים treat הערמה as worse, so a ruling about trickery cannot be applied to a plain sinner.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs that food cooked without an עירוב is forbidden have been pushed away. The ברייתא's silence proves nothing, and the strict rule about הערמה is special to trickery.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You are speaking of trickery —
trickery is different,
for the Sages were more stringent with it than with one who acts intentionally.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הַעֲרָמָה קָא אָמְרַתְּ, שָׁאנֵי הַעֲרָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא in steps 3–4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the הערמה clause of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treats trickery as a milder case than open sinning, but the חכמים were actually stricter about it, so it cannot teach us about a מזיד.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: That ברייתא follows חנניה's view of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a second rejection of the proof. The ברייתא that forbids the food follows חנניה's version of בית שמאי, so it is not the accepted הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is חנניה's, and it follows בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another way to push away the proof from step 4. He says that ברייתא was taught by חנניה according to בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי rejected the proof by saying הערמה is a special case. רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects it a different way: the whole ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who are strict about עירוב תבשילין. So it tells us nothing about the הלכה, which follows בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? The גמרא uses this to name the author of a source.
A תנא who reports what בית שמאי held
The school of שמאי. Their view is usually stricter, and we usually do not rule like them.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
This one, whose view is it?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from step 4, which said the food is forbidden if he used הערמה.

phrases.english: It is Chananya's,
and it follows the view of Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי — חֲנַנְיָה הִיא, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate rejection of the step 4 proof, alongside רב אשי's rejection in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole ברייתא as a source for the accepted halacha.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא follows בית שמאי's strict view, and the הלכה follows בית הלל.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing how strict בית שמאי are about עירוב תבשילין
steps.stepSummary: Support for רב נחמן בר יצחק: according to חנניה, בית שמאי need a separate עירוב for baking, for cooking and for insulating. בית הלל say one cooked dish covers everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: חנניה says that בית שמאי say: One may not bake unless he made the עירוב with bread. One may not cook unless he made the עירוב with a cooked dish. One may not insulate unless hot food was already insulated from ערב יום טוב. בית הלל say: He makes the עירוב with one cooked dish and uses it for all his needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to back up רב נחמן בר יצחק. It shows that בית שמאי, as reported by חנניה, are very strict about עירוב תבשילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי require a matching עירוב for each type of work: bread for baking, a cooked dish for cooking, and hot insulated food for insulating. Since they are this strict, it makes sense that they would also forbid the food after the fact. בית הלל are lenient, so the strict ברייתא does not show what the halacha is.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא. It brings a source to support what was just said.
Insulating food, wrapping it so it stays hot
Hot food that is already insulated
All his needs: baking, cooking and insulating

steps.whatToRemember: The strict ruling that forbids the food may belong to בית שמאי, not to the הלכה.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Chananya says,
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹפִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּפַת,
phrases.english: one may not bake unless he made the eruv with bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּתַבְשִׁיל,
phrases.english: and one may not cook unless he made the eruv with a cooked dish,
and one may not insulate food

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיוּ חַמִּין טְמוּנִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: unless there was hot food already insulated from the day before the Festival.
And Beit Hillel say:
he makes the eruv with one cooked dish,
and uses it for all his needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, חֲנַנְיָה אוֹמֵר, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that shows חנניה reports a strict בית שמאי view, supporting step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That חנניה's version of בית שמאי is strict about עירוב תבשילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which חנניה quotes בית שמאי and contrasts them with בית הלל.

steps.title: New proof from a משנה about tithing produce on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Someone who tithes his produce on שבת may eat it if he did so by mistake, but not if he did so on purpose. This suggests that a forbidden act done on purpose forbids its result.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: If someone tithes his produce on שבת, if he did it by mistake he may eat it. If he did it on purpose, he may not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for the main question. It brings a משנה about someone who tithed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithing on שבת is forbidden. The משנה says that if he did it on purpose, he may not eat the produce. So maybe the same applies to someone who cooks on purpose without an עירוב: the food would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One who separates מעשרות, the tithes, from his produce
By mistake, without meaning to sin
On purpose, knowing it is forbidden

phrases.english: We learned:
phrases.notes: This word is in round brackets, so some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: One who tithes his produce on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he may eat it;
if on purpose, he may not eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְעַשֵּׂר פֵּירוֹתָיו בְּשַׁבָּת, בְּשׁוֹגֵג — יֹאכַל, בְּמֵזִיד — לֹא יֹאכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a fresh source.
steps.raayaObject: That a forbidden act done on purpose makes its result forbidden, so food cooked without an עירוב would be forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about tithing produce on שבת.

steps.title: Rejection: He has other produce to eat
steps.stepSummary: The tithing case is about someone who has other produce, so forbidding this produce costs him little. That does not prove the same for someone cooking without an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is needed for a case where he has other produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the tithing משנה. It says that case is about a person who has other food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he has other produce, forbidding this produce does not hurt him much, so the חכמים could be strict. Someone who did not make an עירוב may have nothing to eat for שבת, so the חכמים might be lenient with him. The two cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for a specific case. It limits a source to a narrow situation.

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
where he has other produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ פֵּירֵי אַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 8 by narrowing the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the tithing משנה to a case where he has other produce.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tithing case causes little loss, unlike someone who has no food prepared for שבת.

steps.title: Another proof: immersing vessels on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Someone who immerses his vessels on שבת may use them if he did so by mistake, but not if he did so on purpose. Again, a forbidden act done on purpose forbids its result.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone immerses his vessels on שבת, if he did it by mistake he may use them. If he did it on purpose, he may not use them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings yet another proof that something produced by a forbidden act done on purpose becomes forbidden. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will respond to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing vessels in a מקוה on שבת is forbidden by the חכמים. If he did it on purpose, he may not use the vessels, even though they are now טהור. This looks like a direct model for food cooked on purpose without an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. It introduces a new source as a proof.
One who immerses something in a מקוה to make it טהור

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who immerses his vessels on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he may use them;
if on purpose, he may not use them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the tithing proof was rejected, the גמרא tries another similar source.
steps.raayaObject: That the result of a forbidden act done on purpose is forbidden, so food cooked without an עירוב would be forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source about immersing vessels on שבת.

steps.title: The vessels case is different: he has other vessels or can borrow
steps.stepSummary: The proof from immersing vessels on שבת is rejected. There the person has other vessels or can borrow some, so forbidding these vessels costs him little.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, that rule is needed for a case where he has other vessels. Or else, he can manage by borrowing vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from Step 10. Forbidding the vessels is no big loss there, so it says nothing about food cooked without an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who immersed vessels on purpose can easily use other vessels or borrow some. Food for שבת is harder to get from others. So the חכמים might be lenient about the food even though they were strict about the vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for… (the rule is talking about a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
where he has other vessels.
phrases.notes: This answers Step 10, the case of someone who immersed his vessels on שבת.

phrases.english: Alternatively, it is possible by borrowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ מָאנֵי אַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from immersing vessels in the same way Step 9 rejected the proof from tithing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from immersing vessels on שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There the loss is small, because he has other vessels or can borrow. Food made without an עירוב may be a harder case.

steps.title: Another proof: cooking on שבת by mistake versus on purpose
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says food cooked on שבת may be eaten if it was cooked by mistake, but not if it was cooked on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one who cooks on שבת, if by mistake, he may eat it. If on purpose, he may not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another proof that a forbidden act done on purpose forbids its result. This time the case is cooking itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is closer to ours, because it is also about cooked food. Food is not something you can simply borrow, so the earlier rejections do not seem to apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is being brought)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who cooks on Shabbat,
if by mistake, he may eat it;
if on purpose, he may not eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof after the vessels proof was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That food cooked on purpose without an עירוב תבשילין is forbidden to eat
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about cooking on שבת

steps.title: שבת is a stricter prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected because breaking שבת is a much more serious sin, so it gets a stronger penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition of שבת is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from cooking on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking שבת is a very severe sin, so a strict penalty fits there. Cooking on יום טוב for the next day without an עירוב is a lighter matter. The question is left unresolved.

phrases.english: The prohibition of Shabbat is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from cooking on שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שבת is more severe than the rabbinic rule of עירוב תבשילין, so you cannot learn one from the other.
steps.whatToRemember: Every proof was rejected. Tithing and vessels involve only a small loss, and שבת is a stricter sin. So the question about food cooked without an עירוב on purpose stays open.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow this other תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, where בית שמאי require two dishes, and says it does not match a different תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: two cooked dishes. Our משנה is not like this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and sets up a contrast with a ברייתא it will bring next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, בית שמאי need two dishes and בית הלל need only one. The גמרא is announcing that another תנא tells the dispute differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the משנה period

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: two cooked dishes.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. There בית הלל say one dish is enough.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not like this tanna,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of eating the food and goes back to the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה follows a different version of the dispute from the one taught in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says both sides agree that two dishes are needed. They argue only about a fish with an egg on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that two dishes are needed. What do they argue about? A fish with an egg on it. בית שמאי say it must be two dishes. בית הלל say this one dish is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that tells the dispute differently from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, even בית הלל usually require two dishes. The argument is only about a fish with an egg on top. בית הלל count it as enough even though it is one dish, and בית שמאי do not.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A fish with an egg on top of it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In our משנה בית הלל say one dish is enough. In this ברייתא both sides usually need two, and they argue only about the fish with the egg.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
that two cooked dishes are needed.
About what did they disagree?
About a fish with an egg on it,
for Beit Shammai say: two cooked dishes,
phrases.notes: This means two real separate dishes. The fish with the egg on it counts as only one.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: one cooked dish.
phrases.notes: This means the fish with the egg on it is enough, even though it is one dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source of the other version mentioned in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides usually need two dishes. They argue only about a fish with an egg on it.

steps.title: Both agree when the egg or leeks are mixed into the fish
steps.stepSummary: If a sliced egg or mashed leeks are put inside the fish, everyone agrees it counts as two dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that if he sliced an egg and put it inside the fish, or mashed leeks and put them inside the fish, they are two dishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a case where בית שמאי and בית הלל agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg lying on top of the fish is in dispute. Once the egg or leeks are prepared and put inside the fish, even בית שמאי count it as two dishes.

phrases.english: And they agree that if he sliced an egg
and put it inside the fish,
or if he mashed leeks
and put them inside the fish,
that they are two cooked dishes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא with a case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sliced egg or mashed leeks put inside the fish count as two dishes according to everyone.

steps.title: רבא rules like our משנה and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like our משנה's version, and like בית הלל: one cooked dish is enough for an עירוב תבשילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows our תנא, according to בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final ruling on the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא picks our משנה's version over רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version. Within that version, he rules like בית הלל, so one cooked dish is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא (the one in our משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is that one cooked dish is enough for an עירוב תבשילין, following our משנה and בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: one cooked dish is enough to make an עירוב תבשילין.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halacha follows our tanna,
and according to Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two versions of the dispute in Steps 14 to 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows our משנה and בית הלל: one cooked dish is enough for an עירוב תבשילין.

steps.title: If the עירוב is eaten after you started, you may finish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the עירוב was eaten or lost, you may not cook relying on it. אביי adds a tradition: if you already began kneading and only then the עירוב was eaten, you may finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he ate the עירוב or it was lost, he may not cook relying on it. אביי said: We have a tradition that if he began his dough and then his עירוב was eaten, he may finish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. אביי then explains one detail: what happens when the עירוב disappears in the middle of the cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says you cannot start cooking for שבת once the עירוב is gone. אביי teaches that if you started while the עירוב still existed, you may complete what you began. The start is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: he ate it or it was lost

steps.whatToRemember: The עירוב must exist when you begin cooking for שבת. If it is eaten after you began, you may finish.

phrases.english: If he ate it or it was lost —
phrases.notes: "It" is the cooked food set aside as the עירוב תבשילין.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יְבַשֵּׁל עָלָיו וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: he may not cook relying on it, etc.
Abaye said: We have a tradition:
if he began working on his dough
and then his eiruv was eaten, he may finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ruling on how many dishes are needed, the גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה about a lost עירוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once you begin cooking with a valid עירוב, losing the עירוב afterward does not stop you from finishing.

steps.title: Immersing when יום טוב falls right after שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: when יום טוב is on Sunday, בית שמאי say everything must be immersed before שבת. בית הלל say כלים must be immersed before שבת, but a person may immerse on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If יום טוב falls right after שבת: בית שמאי say everything must be immersed before שבת. בית הלל say vessels must be immersed before שבת, but a person may immerse on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks when a person and his כלים may be immersed to become טהור for a יום טוב that comes right after שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no time left on Sunday before יום טוב, so the immersion must happen earlier. בית שמאי treat people and כלים the same. בית הלל split them: כלים must be immersed before שבת, while a person may immerse even on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: we immerse, in a מקוה, to become טהור

steps.confusionAlert: Even בית הלל do not allow immersing כלים on שבת. Their leniency covers only a person.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If the festival falls right after Shabbat —
Beit Shammai say:
We immerse everything before Shabbat.
And Beit Hillel say:
Vessels before Shabbat,
and a person on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts a new משנה on a new topic, immersion before יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, כלים must be immersed before שבת, but a person may immerse on שבת. According to בית שמאי, everything must be immersed before שבת.

steps.title: Where both sides agree about purifying on שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree that טמא water in a stone vessel may be made טהור on שבת by touching it to מקוה water. This is not called immersing. They also agree that on יום טוב one may immerse "from גב to גב" and "from חבורה to חבורה."
steps.simpleTranslation: Both agree that we may let water touch other water, in a stone vessel, to make it טהור, but we may not immerse it. We may also immerse from גב to גב and from חבורה to חבורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists cases where בית שמאי and בית הלל agree on what is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making water טהור by letting it touch מקוה water is allowed, because that is not a real immersion. Real immersion stays forbidden. The phrases "from גב to גב" and "from חבורה to חבורה" are left for the גמרא to explain later.

keyTerms.meaning: we let one body of water touch another, a "kiss" of the waters
a stone vessel, which does not become טמא
from one גב to another, explained later in the גמרא

steps.confusionAlert: השקה, letting the waters touch, is different from טבילה, immersion. The משנה permits only the first.

phrases.english: And they agree that we may let the water touch other water
in a stone vessel, to make it pure,
phrases.notes: A stone vessel cannot become טמא, so only the water inside it needs to become טהור.

phrases.english: but we may not immerse.
And we may immerse from one gav to another
and from one group to another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the same משנה with cases where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: השקה of water in a stone vessel is allowed, but immersion is not. Immersing from גב to גב and from חבורה to חבורה is allowed.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no immersing vessels on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree a כלי may not be immersed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, according to everyone, a vessel on שבת is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out a point the משנה implies: on this, both sides agree. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides argued only about a person. Both require כלים to be immersed before שבת. So the ban on immersing a כלי on שבת is shared by everyone, and the גמרא wants to know its source.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
In any case, according to everyone —
phrases.notes: "Everyone" here means both בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.english: a vessel on Shabbat, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת כְּלִי בְּשַׁבָּת לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא reads a point of agreement out of the משנה in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree that a כלי may not be immersed on שבת.

steps.title: Why can't vessels be immersed on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for forbidding the immersion of a כלי on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ban it just pointed out. This sets up רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dipping a כלי in water does not look like one of the מלאכות of שבת. So the גמרא wants to know why it is forbidden.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This asks for the reason behind the agreement noted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis for forbidding the immersion of a כלי on שבת?

steps.title: רבה begins: it is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ban is a גזרה, a protective rule made by the חכמים. The details continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a גזרה...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins answering: the ban comes from the חכמים, not from the תורה. The explanation of what the גזרה protects against continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it a גזרה tells us that immersing a כלי is not itself a תורה-level מלאכה. The חכמים forbade it to prevent some other problem, which רבה explains next.

keyTerms.meaning: a protective decree of the חכמים

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is a decree

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban is a rabbinic גזרה. Its exact reason continues beyond this section.
